internal/httpapi/portal.go:308-352 control-flow rewrite is behaviour-preserving for the success path. Old code set `supplierID = &id` even when the suppliers INSERT failed (id was ""), but the following `if err == nil` guards skipped every use, so no observable change; the new early returns just make each failure name its own key. hashPassword is still reached in exactly the same cases, so no new bcrypt cost on a failed supplier insert. `*supplierID` is non-nil on both paths into the users INSERT (either read from the invitation or assigned after a successful RETURNING).

internal/db/migrations/001_initial.sql:13 `email text NOT NULL UNIQUE` means Postgres names the constraint `users_email_key`, which is what duplicateUserEmail matches; grep found no other index or constraint in the schema whose name contains that string, and users has no deleted_at, so there is no soft-deleted row that could produce a 409 for an address the admin cannot see in the list.

internal/httpapi/suppliers.go:670 duplicateUserEmail matches on `strings.Contains(fmt.Sprint(err), "users_email_key")` rather than unwrapping *pgconn.PgError and checking Code=="23505" + ConstraintName. Fragile if the constraint is ever renamed, but it mirrors the pre-existing duplicateBusinessNumber on line 659, so it is consistent with the codebase rather than a new pattern. Not a merge blocker; worth tightening if either helper is touched again.

internal/httpapi/portal.go:346 the 409 email_registered discloses that an address has an account, but only to someone already holding a valid unconsumed invitation carrying that exact address, so it is not an enumeration vector. createUser's 409 is admin-only.
No migrations, no data backfill, no external state — the change is three Go files plus frontend and is a clean `git revert`.

Scope is tight: the only edits outside the two error paths are logDB(err) on the pre-existing save_failed/registration_failed tails and `export` on SupplierRegistration in web/src/App.tsx:185, which self-register.test.tsx needs to render it. No refactors, formatting sweeps or dependency bumps ride along.
